protocols.label: Bone sarcoma (osteosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, chondrosarcoma)
protocols.note: DRAFT, not approved for real use: needs a clinician's check. Configurable by the clinical team. Required records transcribed from the NCG Guidelines for Bone and Soft Tissue Tumours (2019) (National Cancer Grid, India), the bone sarcoma pages (evaluation p 4, osteosarcoma p 7, Ewing sarcoma p 12, chondrosarcoma p 17, appendices p 25 to 40; the PDF page is the printed page), each with its verbatim quote and page. Tiers printed by NCG are kept; the tiers whose tier_basis says 'proposed' are proposals, to be confirmed by the hospital Tumour Board (clinical review before real use). A record NCG gives only under a condition the system never judges (a finding, a plan) is shown with NCG's own tier and the condition, never counted. The stage and the risk group are as recorded by the clinician, never computed. Nothing here suggests treatment. There are three settings because the work-up differs: the chondrosarcoma flow has no alkaline phosphatase and LDH, no immunohistochemistry and no baseline organ tests, and prints the bone scan as Optional. The book has no Enneking and no bone-specific stage table. Echocardiogram and audiometry before chemotherapy are one line of the book (p 28), listed as separate records so each goes to the team that does it. Ewing sarcoma and osteosarcoma are not in the paediatric book. A child's treating team is Paediatric Oncology: clinical records go to the owner of the Case File.

protocols.label: Brain and CNS tumours
protocols.note: DRAFT, not approved for real use: needs a clinician's check, and the child setting needs it even more than the rest. The National Cancer Grid has no brain or CNS guideline and no Indian national guideline for brain tumours was found, so the adult records come from a European guideline: the EANO guidelines on the diagnosis and treatment of diffuse gliomas of adulthood (Weller et al., Nature Reviews Clinical Oncology 2021;18:170-186, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41571-020-00447-z), open access under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/; the licence line was read on the PDF and is logged beside it). Selected sentences are quoted verbatim, each with its PDF page (journal page = PDF page + 169); the labels, the tiers and the routing are this draft's own. The guideline rests on the WHO 2016 classification and the cIMPACT-NOW updates and is not Indian; the Indian ISNO papers were not used because their reuse terms are not confirmed. Tiers: EANO uses classes of evidence and levels of recommendation, so one rule maps them. Level A or B for a record the text asks for in every patient is a (Essential, a proposal). The same test asked only in a subgroup the system never judges (a negative IDH1 stain, retained ATRX, glioblastoma, midline location) is system tier c with the condition shown, never counted. A sentence with no level (the post-operative MRI) is a proposed b. All tiers are proposals, to be confirmed by the hospital Tumour Board (clinical review before real use). The guideline has no line on CSF or spinal imaging for diffuse gliomas, so none is listed. No treatment line is copied; the system never grades or stages. Brain metastases of another cancer belong to that cancer's checklist. For a child the NCG paediatric book has no brain tumour chapter (it names the brain only as a screening MRI in retinoblastoma and as CNS spread in leukaemia and lymphoma), so the child setting reuses the same records.

settings.label: Other adult brain or CNS tumour (for example meningioma or metastasis), as recorded
Child with a brain or CNS tumour, as recorded

protocols.label: Cancer of Unknown Primary (CUP)
protocols.note: DRAFT, not approved for real use. Configurable by the clinical team. Required records derived from NICE CG104 (metastatic malignant disease of unknown primary origin in adults, 2010, last updated 26 April 2023, reviewed 16 July 2025 with no change) and the ESMO 2023 cancer of unknown primary guideline (Kramer et al.), quoted verbatim with the section or page on every record. No Indian source exists: NCG India has no CUP guideline, and neither ICMR, TMC nor the MoHFW STGs cover it (owner, 17 Oct 2026). Where NICE and ESMO differ (mammography, tumour markers) the owner chose NICE (R05-Q07). The checklist grows with the NICE diagnostic phase the doctor records (MUO, provisional CUP, confirmed CUP). Nothing here computes a stage, names a likely primary or suggests treatment. To be confirmed by a named doctor and the hospital Tumour Board (clinical review before real use). ESMO page numbers are the PDF page numbers (1 to 19) as the guideline library reads the file; the journal page is given under where.

settings.label: MUO (malignancy of undefined primary origin), as recorded
settings.definition: Metastatic malignancy identified on the basis of a limited number of tests, without an obvious primary site, before comprehensive investigation.
settings.definition_source: NICE CG104, Terms used in this guideline: malignancy of undefined primary origin (MUO)

settings.label: Provisional CUP (after the initial screen, before specialist review), as recorded
settings.definition: Metastatic epithelial or neuro-endocrine malignancy identified on the basis of histology or cytology, with no primary site detected despite a selected initial screen of investigations, before specialist review and possible further specialised investigations.
settings.definition_source: NICE CG104, Terms used in this guideline: provisional carcinoma of unknown primary origin (provisional CUP)

settings.label: Confirmed CUP (after specialist review and special investigations), as recorded
settings.definition: Metastatic epithelial or neuro-endocrine malignancy identified on the basis of final histology, with no primary site detected despite a selected initial screen of investigations, specialist review, and further specialised investigations as appropriate.
settings.definition_source: NICE CG104, Terms used in this guideline: confirmed carcinoma of unknown primary origin (confirmed CUP)

protocols.label: Leukaemia (acute and chronic)

The adult flow charts are pictures with no text layer: their lines were read with the project's own OCR engine (Tesseract) and each such quote is marked ocr and checked against that engine's reading of the page. Four settings group the diseases: where two diseases of one setting carry different letters, the record keeps the higher and its tier_basis names both. Child APML is in the child acute setting, child CML in the child chronic setting. Tiers printed by NCG are kept; the tiers whose tier_basis says 'proposed' are proposals, to be confirmed by the hospital Tumour Board (clinical review before real use). Leukaemia has no stage: the risk group or phase (for example AML favourable, intermediate or poor risk; CML chronic, accelerated or blast phase) is as recorded in a report, never computed; risk scores are never calculated. Langerhans cell histiocytosis is not in this checklist. Nothing here suggests treatment. India first: the National Cancer Grid books are the only source (the adult book points to the ICMR guideline for flow cytometry quality control, page 91).
